name: R113 exact C descriptor/frame receive boundary
priority: Fix inherited FD misassociation before any further performance acceptance. No claim that previous read-ahead CPU wins preserve all C semantics.
algorithm: recvmsg only the remaining bytes of the current 12-byte prefix. Accept ancillary only while no descriptor is pending.
Once prefix is validated, read only the remaining body of that frame using read, which discards ancillary as in C. Never consume into a following frame.
Keep event-loop stack scratch for small frames, exact owned residual bytes across readiness, and existing LargeFrame owned body for large messages.
Replace rx_fds end markers with one pending_fd; remove rx_drained cross-frame shortcut and obsolete rx_start compaction state.
Preserve owned InMsg/server API, R111 borrow reuse, R112 Box table, all output optimizations and corrected epoch/ACL/queue behavior.
excluded: Do not simply reassign a descriptor to the first buffered frame: a preceding plain frame is the counterexample.
Do not use MSG_PEEK absence of cmsg/MSG_CTRUNC as a safe FD-free predicate: Linux scm_fp_dup allocation failure can hide ancillary on peek.
No borrowed dispatch, touched optimization or system-object allocation changes in the correctness fix.
validation: Add failing receive regression for bundled first-frame FD and preceding plain frame before implementing.
Preserve and adapt residual, batching, large frame, fragmented prefix, fd ownership/drop, malformed length and EOF tests; add body-only FD discard and first-prefix-FD preservation.
Reproduce the new normalized wireprobe FD scenario against exact C and the known bad R112; fixed candidate must match C on physical router.
Run 41 existing Linux unit tests plus new cases, seven existing router protocol groups and six functional/recovery gates before resuming performance.
Re-freeze all performance identities and report any lost read-ahead advantage. R112-only performance plan is superseded before sampling.
